Ulashkivtsi New Jewish Сemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopil Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. In 1906, a memorial to Theodor Herzl, founder of political Zionism, was erected inside Ulashkivtsi's own synagogue — a notable act of formal commemoration within a religious space. The town's Jewish population had collapsed from 489 in 1900 to just 138 (0.6 percent of the town) by 1921. In June 1941, a pogrom staged by local Ukrainians claimed the lives of 68 Jews and saw their property pillaged; survivors fled to Chortkiv and other nearby localities. This is the newer of Ulashkivtsi's two Jewish cemeteries, existing by the mid-19th century, per epigraphic data.
